answer: Each new agent locks a bond in a protocol vault for several epochs before rewards vest. While locked, the network publishes a public mirror of every action digest and clusters near-duplicates; matched farms are slashed and the bonds burned. An identity must also accumulate a unique willow of counterparties—a branching set of independent partners—because sharing the same narrow partner set is treated as one controller. An attacker therefore posts a fresh bond, waits out the lock, and builds a distinct partner tree for every extra key, or loses the deposits.
